title: Health & Wellness Seminar - Eyes Wide Open: The Secrets of Sight and the Business Behind Your Care
location: 2003 male United States Presidential Scholar for the state of Georgia. Afterward, Dr. Hollar enrolled in the Duke University School of Medicine where he received his Doctor of Medicine (M.D.) degree a
description: How is an optician different from an optometrist and when do you need an ophthalmologist? Which eye diseases steal vision silently, which warning signs cannot wait, and what can today’s cataract surgeries really accomplish? In this presentation, ophthalmologist Matthew Hollar, MD, will explore eye health from cataracts, glaucoma, macular degeneration, and retinal emergencies, while revealing the remarkable technologies now preserving and restoring sight. He will also cover on how insurance, consolidation, and corporate ownership are transforming the relationship among patients, physicians, and the businesses that deliver care, what these changes can improve, what they may put at risk, and how you can become a wiser healthcare consumer. Come find out who's really watching your eyes. Presented by: Dr. Matthew Hollar Dr. Matthew Hollar joined the team of comprehensive ophthalmologists at North Georgia Eye Clinic in 2016, specializing in medical and surgical care of the eye. A native of western North Carolina, he and his family have lived north of Atlanta since 1999. title: Small Business Seminar - Expanding Small Business Capabilities through Higher Education Partnerships
description: About the presentation: Small businesses may fail to scale due to lack of access to resources. Often times, partnering with local technical colleges and universities is not included in discussions when exploring options to scale a business. However, technical colleges and universities are a good resource for small businesses seeking talent, development, and funding support. This session will highlight various ways that small businesses can expand capabilities by partnering with higher education institutions to build a talent pipeline, provide upskilling opportunities for current employees, and to pursue research and grant funding. About the speaker: Dr. Shatrela Washington-Hubbard serves as the Swinton A. Griffith III Dean of the Jacobs College of Business & Media at Brenau University. She holds an earned doctor of philosophy in learning, leadership, and organization development from the University of Georgia. Her professional experience includes industry experience in the fields of human resources and education. Dr. Washington-Hubbard’s research agenda focuses on topics in entrepreneurship, experiential learning, and career development. 8:15 - 8:30 AM Networking 8:30 - 9:30 AM Sem

title: Leadership & AI Forum
description: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing the way businesses operate, market themselves, make decisions, and prepare for the future. Join the Greater Hall Chamber of Commerce for our Leadership & AI Forum , a panel discussion designed to help local business leaders understand how AI can be applied strategically and responsibly in today's business environment. Hear from experts representing higher education, small business development, and digital marketing as they discuss practical applications of AI, emerging opportunities, potential challenges, and what business leaders should be considering as AI continues to evolve. Whether your organization is already incorporating AI into its operations or you're still exploring where to begin, this forum will provide actionable insights to help you navigate the changing landscape. description: Farm City Breakfast Wednesday November 18, 2026 7:30am North Hall Community Center This event highlights agribusiness is the Hall County area and is a partnership between the UGA/Hall County Extension, Georgia Farm Bureau and the Greater Hall Chamber of Commerce. This years special guest is Ag Commissioner Tyler Harper. Tyler J Harper is Georgia’s 17th Agriculture Commissioner, a 7th generation farmer, a small businessman, and a proud native of rural South Georgia. A lifelong resident of the Peach State, Harper is a champion for Georgia’s #1 industry, the farm families who fuel its success, and all of rural Georgia. He knows that for Georgia’s farmers and producers, agriculture is more than just a job or a hobby – it is our way of life. Harper grows peanuts, cotton, and timber and runs a small cow-calf operation on land that has been in his family for over 100 years in Irwin County, Georgia.
